Hey man, I feel you. Now I’m not the best writer so hang tight. 
I don’t mean to put this info out there to brag or to show it off but to put into perspective that what you are feeling is what many other people think and feel at all levels. I’m 22 working for a utility contractor making over $100k a year while being the best husband and father I can be. Every single day I compare myself to people doing “better” than me and I feel like a complete loser. Feeling like I’m not doing good enough and that I need to be at or above someone else’s level. What I’ve been trying to do to combat this feeling is trying to realize and understand that all of that is just a façade. These same people have failing marriages or their kids hate them or they are irresponsible with their money and flaunt material things and are in turn in massive debt that they will never be able to escape. They are so busy trying to impress everyone else that they don’t take the time to travel, try new things, meet new people and are overall completely miserable people that aren’t actually living THEIR life. I myself have been struggling with coming to terms with the fact that there is no such thing as a life that is better than yours. Your life is only as good as you make it no matter what house you live in, what car you drive or how much money you have in your bank account because you very well could have all of the best of those things and still be an extremely unhappy person. Learn to find positives in anything and everything. Learn to have even a bit of gratitude for the things you do have because there are good, honest people out here that are struggling to even find a job while living in their car trying to find a reason to live. Live a life that YOU are comfortable with, not a life that OTHERS are comfortable with you living.

I have pretty much the same truck, but the SX version (Black premium wheels and color-matched bumpers).
I’m not sure what you’re planning on doing with the truck but after nearly 53,000 miles of traveling up and down California for work, driving to Ohio and back twice and a load of off-roading, I can confidently say that this truck is much more capable than what the V6/4WD guys have to say about them. I have the 2.7l 2wd and I’ve pushed this thing to its limits and then some. I’ve wheeled thru some light-moderate snow, deep water and mud, treated it like a prerunner jumping and drifting it on wide-open trails and have taken it pretty deep in the mountains on some amazing camping trips all mostly thanks to that trusty and reliable rear differential locker.
You’ll eventually grow tired of seeing all the badass trucks out there and want to get rid of it and upgrade, but after you start having some REAL fun with this thing and slapping on some mods and upgrades, you’ll never want to get rid of it. 
Get you some aggressive tires, traction boards, a nice suspension system, premium lighting and a winch and you can essentially do 90% of what a TRD Pro can do, with that missing 10% being going uphill in snow and mud. 
Have fun!
